newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Italian debt vols continue downward path.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Italian debt vols continue downward path.

text.p: (Lisa Wilson, reporting from the LIFFE floor)

Implied volatility of Italian BTP and Eurolira options remained on a downward track on Wednesday, amid conflicting signals about Italy's role in European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU), traders said.
"Volatility is still heading down, although it's still relatively expensive compared to other European markets," said a broker at a British brokerage on LIFFE.
"It's already pricing in as much uncertainty about EMU as the market feels. I don't think it can go up on this new EMU talk."
Bundesbank council member Ernst Welteke said on Wednesday that sustainable low budget deficits were more important than the three percent deficit to GDP ratio required for EMU.
He later said it was important to take all criteria into account, including debt targets which some "small countries" have a problem with.
Earlier in the week, a European Commission report warned Italy it was not doing enough to ensure it would meet the convergence criteria for EMU.
The broker said volatility for Eurolira and BTPs was likely to fall further as the Italian markets regained their poise.
June Eurolira volatility was quoted at 17 percent middle. September volatility was also 17 percent, down from 17.1 percent on Tuesday, while December was off the same amount at 18 percent.
June Eurolira futures were up five basis points at 93.27 by 1129 GMT. June BTP futures were up 52 basis points at 130.08
Paper was observed selling upside calls in Eurolira and calendar call spreads were notable at 93.50/93.75 in June.
More than 2,000 contracts had traded at the 93.50 strike by 1016 GMT and more than 1,200 at the 93.75 strike.
September and December saw limited activity clustered around the 93.75 strike. Traders said the Eurolira pit was generally short volatility.

In BTPs, June volatility slid to 7.1 percent from 7.2 percent earlier and liquidity appeared to be starting to pick up in September as the June expiry approaches. June BTP futures expire in next Wednesday.
September calls at the 130.00 strike were bought at a volatility of 7.7 percent and volatility had slid from 7.8 percent earlier.
A trader at a French brokerage said the relatively limited ranges being traded by the futures market were contributing to the slide in volatility.
